teaching_promise: Follow one synthetic Harborline incident from a narrow provider ticket to a federated, rights-preserving resilience response that keeps recovery, correction, adaptation, and residual ownership visible.

story.concrete_case: A fictional Harborline benefits-portal impersonation exercise uses synthetic artifacts and no real victims or attack recipes.
story.opening_question: When prevention fails, can cooperating institutions protect people beyond one model provider without converting victims into a surveillance record?
story.payoff: The Harborline network keeps service available, repairs records, learns from a partial miss, and leaves remaining harm with an accountable owner.
story.transfer: Stable capability fields must carry these stage, privacy, dispute, and residual boundaries through model and runtime replacement.

art_direction.visual_thesis: Resilience is a federated state machine whose four verbs remain distinct, overlapping, rights-constrained, and honest about residual harm.
art_direction.signature_image: A Harborline incident envelope routes one synthetic event across providers, agencies, community advocates, service continuity, recovery paths, and a residual ledger.
art_direction.visual_world: A dark civic operations room with a persistent Harborline service frame, colored stage routes, typed role panels, evidence custody boundaries, and readable residual ledgers.
art_direction.composition_rule: Keep the incident or service on the left, accountable routes in the center, and affected-party, remedy, or residual consequences on the right; never flatten them into one score.
art_direction.palette_rule: Gold marks policy and coordination, blue observation and service, green continuity or repair, violet participation or adaptation, red failure or burden, and muted outlines uncertainty; every color is labeled.
art_direction.typography_rule: Use short uppercase labels for typed states and full-sentence narration for their implications; never use a color-only legend or decorative paragraph card.
art_direction.motion_character: Routes assemble, branch, pause, cross, correct, and retain custody; holds are deliberate reading states with an observable incident or service relation.
art_direction.camera_rule: Widen for federated roles and coverage gaps, tighten for an affected path or false-positive repair, and keep the Harborline frame stable across the case trace.
art_direction.surface_rule: Every panel names an authority, stage, population, evidence boundary, or residual; synthetic exercise labels remain visible whenever the case could be mistaken for deployment evidence.
art_direction.ending_image: Harborline remains available while repair, learning, and an owned residual route point forward to stable capability fields.

audio_direction.narration_style: Calm, direct, humane, and operationally precise; concrete Harborline sentences are followed by explicit non-claims.
audio_direction.pacing_arc: Open with a shortfall, build the four-stage contract, widen to the federated envelope, trace Harborline, then slow at residual custody and the evidence ceiling.
audio_direction.music_policy: No music is required; preserve speech intelligibility and the deliberate space around stage transitions and residuals.
audio_direction.sound_effect_policy: No abuse or alarm sound effects; optional restrained interface ticks may mark packet routing only and must never imply empirical success.
audio_direction.duration_rationale: The 06:51.52 runtime intentionally exceeds the preferred soft range so resist, absorb, recover, adapt, privacy custody, false-positive correction, affected paths, and residual ownership remain distinct; six minutes is not a hard cap.

accessibility.color_redundancy: Labels, enclosure, position, arrow direction, line style, and crosses duplicate every color distinction.
accessibility.motion_redundancy: A paused stage or packet retains its labels and relations; understanding never depends on seeing a transition at speed.
accessibility.integrated_description: The adjacent descriptive transcript names Harborline, each stage, authority route, affected path, privacy boundary, correction, and residual state.
accessibility.caption_plan: Captions derive from the exact 29-segment narration receipt and are capped for readable line length without changing words or timing.
accessibility.reduced_motion_assessment: Reduced motion leaves the typed stage diagrams, packet boundaries, crosses, and residual ownership legible even when arrows and fades are minimized.

beats.narration: A model can refuse a harmful request and a provider can close an incident ticket. People can still lose money, access, privacy, or trust when copies, accounts, and narratives move elsewhere.
beats.visual_purpose: Expose the gap between a closed provider ticket and continuing societal harm.
beats.visual_action: Route provider to a closed ticket, then reveal copies, accounts, and trust continuing into a harm panel.
beats.attention_target: The red harm panel outside the provider boundary.
beats.composition: Provider and ticket occupy the left and center; harm and external residues occupy the right.
beats.motion_curve: Slow route followed by a widening reveal of external residues.
beats.camera_action: Widen from the ticket to the harms outside its frame.
beats.hold_purpose: Let the opening mismatch become a testable question.
beats.evidence_boundary: The visual frames a design problem; it does not measure a provider or societal outcome.

beats.narration: Societal resilience asks a wider question: when prevention fails, can cooperating institutions resist, absorb, recover, and adapt without turning a victim into a permanent surveillance record?
beats.visual_purpose: Name the four verbs and the rights constraint.
beats.visual_action: Assemble the four stage badges into a loop with people, services, and rights beneath it.
beats.attention_target: The four-stage loop and rights constraint.
beats.composition: Stages occupy the left-center in sequence; the rights badge anchors the lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Measured sequential assembly with a return arrow.
beats.camera_action: Track across the four stages, then settle on rights.
beats.hold_purpose: Make the contract memorable before applying it.
beats.evidence_boundary: The four verbs are a design framing, not evidence that any intervention protects a population.

beats.narration: The shortcut is one classifier, one takedown queue, or one company playbook. Each sees one surface, inherits blind spots, and can mistake its own clean dashboard for a safe society.
beats.visual_purpose: Show why a single control point cannot stand for societal coverage.
beats.visual_action: Place classifier, takedown, and playbook above private, platform, and harmed-person surfaces; cross the implied whole-society conclusion.
beats.attention_target: Unobserved surfaces below the control points.
beats.composition: Controls line the upper band; surfaces and blind spots occupy the lower band.
beats.motion_curve: Controls appear confidently, then the camera reveals the unobserved lower band.
beats.camera_action: Tilt down from local dashboards to external surfaces.
on_screen_text: ONE CONTROL POINT HAS BLIND SPOTS
beats.hold_purpose: Make blind-spot migration visible rather than rhetorical.
beats.evidence_boundary: Control-point limits motivate layered coverage; they do not show that a proposed network prevents harm.

beats.narration: Use one low-risk synthetic class: a fictional Harborline benefits-portal impersonation that sends people toward a false instruction. The exercise names no real victim, target, or attack recipe.
beats.visual_purpose: Introduce a safe, bounded worked case.
beats.visual_action: Connect a real Harborline service panel to a crossed false instruction and label the fixture synthetic only.
beats.attention_target: The synthetic-only boundary around the case.
beats.composition: The service is left, false instruction center, and synthetic boundary lower right.
beats.motion_curve: A single red relation appears, then the safety boundary settles.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on the synthetic fixture after revealing the service.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent the exercise from being mistaken for an attack recipe or deployment result.
beats.evidence_boundary: Harborline is a fictional teaching fixture; it is not an observed incident or efficacy study.

beats.narration: Start with resist: scoped access controls, friction on high-risk actions, provenance, education, and defensive review make harmful action harder while preserving legitimate access.
beats.visual_purpose: Show resistance as a layered defense with a legitimate-access objective.
beats.visual_action: Fan threat into access, friction, provenance, education, and review, then route to legitimate access.
beats.attention_target: The transition from threat to bounded controls to legitimate access.
beats.object_before: A Harborline harm pathway before layered resistance
beats.composition: Threat anchors left; controls form a central vertical stack; legitimate access is right.
beats.motion_curve: Fan-out followed by a single bounded destination.
beats.camera_action: Hold the control stack while the destination appears.
beats.hold_purpose: Separate layered resistance from a one-number safety claim.
beats.evidence_boundary: The control stack is a design requirement; it does not establish intervention effectiveness.

beats.narration: Resistance is not a score. Every control names threat, population, language, channel, threshold, latency, expiry, and the legitimate users it might burden.
beats.visual_purpose: Bind every control to scope and burden fields.
beats.visual_action: Attach typed scope fields to a control and route the record to a legitimate-user burden marker.
beats.attention_target: The burden field beside the control specification.
beats.composition: Control left, scope fields center, burden lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Fields attach one by one, ending in a red burden marker.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on scope labels rather than the red marker alone.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep unequal burden in the same frame as defensive capability.
beats.evidence_boundary: Recording scope and burden does not prove equal coverage or harmless friction.

beats.narration: Absorb means essential functions continue: the real Harborline service has manual fallback, trusted contact routes, segregated operations, and human surge capacity while the signal is investigated.
beats.visual_purpose: Define absorption as continuity for people rather than provider uptime alone.
beats.visual_action: Route the Harborline service into manual fallback, trusted contact, segregated operations, and human surge nodes.
beats.attention_target: Continuity nodes that keep the service available.
beats.composition: Service left, continuity nodes center, continuity outcome lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Controlled fan-out with a calm settle.
beats.camera_action: Widen enough to show all four fallback paths.
beats.hold_purpose: Make continuity a multi-party obligation.
beats.evidence_boundary: The fallback design does not show that Harborline or any real service would remain available.

beats.narration: Recover is broader than removal. Contain reachable accounts, preserve evidence, notify affected people, correct the record, restore service, and open remedy for harms that cannot be undone.
beats.visual_purpose: Turn recovery into separately measured affected-party paths.
beats.visual_action: Route an incident into containment, preservation, notification, correction, restoration, and remedy, then check terminal paths.
beats.attention_target: The remedy and terminal-path boundary.
beats.composition: Incident left, six recovery paths center, terminal-path assertion right.
beats.motion_curve: Staggered branch sequence ending in a verification hold.
beats.camera_action: Track from incident into the lower remedy path.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent local takedown from masquerading as societal recovery.
beats.evidence_boundary: Recovery fields define obligations and residuals; they do not compel foreign systems or guarantee redress.

beats.narration: Adapt closes the loop: patch controls, change agreements, fund defense, update education, exercise the case, and publish safe lessons without publishing reusable abuse detail.
beats.visual_purpose: Show adaptation as changed defense behavior with safe disclosure.
beats.visual_action: Fan a failure or near miss into patch, agreement, education, exercise, and a safe lesson, ending at new behavior.
beats.attention_target: New field behavior rather than a report sentence.
beats.composition: Failure left, adaptations center, behavior outcome right.
beats.motion_curve: Branch and converge, with a restrained final indication.
beats.camera_action: Widen over the adaptation set, then tighten on behavior.
beats.hold_purpose: Separate adaptation from documentation alone.
beats.evidence_boundary: A changed playbook is not evidence that an adaptation worked across languages, platforms, or jurisdictions.

beats.narration: The four stages overlap. Recovery can reveal new exposure; adaptation can introduce a new failure; resistance continues while people are supported. Closure requires a named owner for every residual.
beats.visual_purpose: Prevent a falsely clean waterfall model.
beats.visual_action: Cycle stages while a new exposure reopens the loop and routes to a residual owner.
beats.attention_target: Reopen and residual-owner routes.
beats.composition: Stages left-center; exposure and owner right, connected by a reopen arrow.
beats.motion_curve: Sequential loop with a sharp reopen branch and calm custody settle.
beats.camera_action: Follow the reopen route instead of leaving the loop.
beats.hold_purpose: Make closure conditional on owned residuals.
beats.evidence_boundary: The loop prevents category collapse in the design; it does not establish complete closure in society.

beats.narration: Shared coordination begins with a federated incident envelope. It carries an incident ID, domain, severity, affected function, confidence, purpose, recipients, disclosure class, and expiry.
beats.visual_purpose: Construct a minimal, routable incident identity.
beats.visual_action: Fan typed routing fields from a shared ID into a bounded packet and end at minimum routing facts.
beats.attention_target: The fields that make sharing purposeful and expiring.
beats.composition: ID left, typed fields center, minimum packet right.
beats.motion_curve: Structured field reveal and bounded convergence.
beats.camera_action: Pan down the field stack, ending on expiry.
beats.hold_purpose: Make the envelope concrete without implying a universal registry.
beats.evidence_boundary: The envelope is a proposed coordination contract, not a deployed data-sharing system.

beats.narration: The envelope is not a universal database. Raw victim material, credentials, medical information, and sensitive defenses remain with the appropriate custodian unless a specific lawful purpose authorizes transfer.
beats.visual_purpose: Make privacy-preserving evidence custody visible.
beats.visual_action: Separate shared routing facts from local custody fields and show a lawful-purpose gate between them.
beats.attention_target: The boundary between shared packet and local sensitive evidence.
beats.composition: Shared packet left, custody right, lawful-purpose gate above.
beats.motion_curve: A route pauses at the gate rather than automatically crossing.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on the gate and sensitive fields.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep privacy and due process in the incident mechanism.
beats.evidence_boundary: The envelope does not decide legal duties, admissibility, privilege, or lawful transfer.

beats.narration: Each participant records what it can do: provider, platform, infrastructure operator, public agency, researcher, civil-society group, or harmed-party advocate. Authority and contact are fields, not assumptions.
beats.visual_purpose: Type the participating roles and their authority boundaries.
beats.visual_action: Route participant role badges to an incident packet while crossing an assumed-power badge.
beats.attention_target: Role-specific authority rather than a central owner.
beats.composition: Roles form a left lattice; packet and crossed assumed power sit right.
beats.motion_curve: Staggered role reveal and parallel route construction.
beats.camera_action: Widen to include civil society and advocates, not only providers.
beats.hold_purpose: Preserve role separation and harmed-party participation.
beats.evidence_boundary: Role fields describe a proposed contract; they do not grant legal authority or ensure participation.

beats.narration: Build a coverage graph. Map each known harm pathway to its observable surfaces, participating organizations, detection signals, response authority, and harmed-party route. An empty edge is a visible residual.
beats.visual_purpose: Expose coverage gaps instead of laundering them into a success metric.
beats.visual_action: Route a harm path through surface, signal, responder, and harmed-party route, ending in a dashed empty edge.
beats.attention_target: The empty edge and its residual label.
beats.composition: Harm path left, operational graph center, empty edge lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Layered graph construction followed by a dashed unresolved route.
beats.camera_action: Widen to show the gap rather than cropping it out.
beats.hold_purpose: Make missing observability and response ownership inspectable.
beats.evidence_boundary: A coverage graph exposes known gaps; it does not prove every harm pathway is known or preventable.

beats.narration: The graph also exposes monoculture. If several detectors share data, model, language, or threshold, their alerts are correlated evidence, not independent confirmation. Migration to another channel remains in scope.
beats.visual_purpose: Show correlated detectors and migration as a common blind spot.
beats.visual_action: Route three detectors into shared data/model/language, cross correlated evidence, and show a dashed other-channel path.
beats.attention_target: Shared dependency beneath apparently independent alerts.
beats.composition: Detectors left, common dependency center, crossed alert and migration right.
beats.motion_curve: Convergent routes reveal common cause before the cross appears.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on the shared dependency, then follow the dashed migration.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent alert counts from becoming false confidence.
beats.evidence_boundary: Correlation and migration are design risks; this visual does not estimate their real-world frequency.

beats.narration: Keep dispute state beside incident state. A report can be credible enough to route while still being unverified; a false intervention needs correction, appeal, and removal of its own downstream residue.
beats.visual_purpose: Separate routing confidence from truth and preserve false-positive repair.
beats.visual_action: Route a report to a not-yet-fact state, then branch a false intervention into appeal, correction, and residue removal.
beats.attention_target: The crossed false intervention and repair paths.
beats.composition: Report left, routing and false intervention center, repair badges right.
beats.motion_curve: Route first, then visibly correct the downstream false state.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on appeal and correction after the cross.
beats.hold_purpose: Preserve due process and correction as part of defense.
beats.evidence_boundary: A dispute-aware packet does not establish truth, innocence, or legal remedy.

beats.narration: Measure stages together: time to detect, contain, notify, restore, correct, and adapt; avoided and repaired harm; false intervention; coverage; accessibility; and total burden.
beats.visual_purpose: Tie operational speed to harm, burden, and access rather than using one metric.
beats.visual_action: Pair each response stage with outcome fields for avoided/repaired harm, false intervention, coverage, accessibility, and burden.
beats.attention_target: The paired stage/outcome columns.
beats.composition: Stage badges left and outcome badges right connected one-to-one.
beats.motion_curve: Regular paired construction with no implied aggregate score.
beats.camera_action: Hold a wide view so total burden remains visible.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep response speed from borrowing the success of recovery or equity.
beats.evidence_boundary: Metric design does not establish that any measured improvement reduces societal harm.

beats.narration: Harborline receives the first synthetic report. A platform sees a suspicious message, the benefits agency sees a call spike, and a community group sees confusion. None owns the whole event.
beats.visual_purpose: Begin the concrete trace with separate observations and no premature owner.
beats.visual_action: Route platform, agency, and community reports into one shared incident identity.
beats.attention_target: The convergence into a shared event.
beats.composition: Three reporters left and center; shared incident right.
beats.motion_curve: Staggered observations converge without assigning global authority.
beats.camera_action: Widen enough to keep all three observers in view.
beats.hold_purpose: Make federation a coordination relation, not centralization.
beats.evidence_boundary: The reporters and event are synthetic teaching objects.

beats.narration: Resist has partial success: provenance and friction slow the false path, but a copied image appears on another service. The right conclusion is not failure or victory; it is a newly observed edge.
beats.visual_purpose: Show how partial defense updates the coverage graph without producing a binary verdict.
beats.visual_action: Route provenance/friction to a slowed false path, then reveal a copied image and dashed new coverage edge.
beats.attention_target: The new edge created by the partial miss.
beats.object_after: Partial success with newly observed gap
beats.composition: Controls left, slowed path center, copied image and edge right.
beats.motion_curve: Success route is crossed by a later residual reveal.
beats.camera_action: Follow the copied-image route after the initial success.
beats.hold_purpose: Reject binary success/failure reasoning for adaptive misuse.
beats.evidence_boundary: The synthetic partial miss does not estimate real bypass rates or intervention value.

beats.narration: Absorb keeps the real benefits service available. Operators route people through a verified channel, hold risky changes for review, and publish an accessible status notice without exposing the false instruction.
beats.visual_purpose: Trace continuity and safe communication during the incident.
beats.visual_action: Route the real service to a verified channel, a risk hold, and an accessible status notice.
beats.attention_target: Continuity and communication without harmful reproduction.
beats.composition: Service left; verified channel and hold center; notice right.
beats.motion_curve: Two safety branches and one communication branch settle together.
beats.camera_action: Keep the service visible while the notice appears.
beats.hold_purpose: Show protection of legitimate users and essential service.
beats.evidence_boundary: The Harborline continuity route is synthetic and does not show actual service availability.

beats.narration: Recover creates an affected-path inventory: people, accounts, transactions, copies, search results, devices, services, and partner organizations. Each path is contained, restored, corrected, notified, disputed, unreachable, or residual.
beats.visual_purpose: Make recovery scope wider than the provider's own surface.
beats.visual_action: Fan the incident into affected paths, then map each path to a typed disposition.
beats.attention_target: The right-hand dispositions, including unreachable and residual.
beats.composition: Incident left, affected entities center, dispositions right.
beats.motion_curve: Dense but orderly fan-out with readable stagger.
beats.camera_action: Widen to include residual and unreachable paths.
on_screen_text: RECOVERY STARTS WITH THE AFFECTED PATHS
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent a local service closure from erasing downstream harm.
beats.evidence_boundary: An inventory records intended custody and outcomes; it does not guarantee restoration or compensation.

beats.narration: A language-access review finds that an automated warning would wrongly block a legitimate Harborline worker. The network lowers the burden, preserves the appeal, and records unequal coverage instead of hiding it in precision.
beats.visual_purpose: Show false-positive correction and unequal coverage as first-class response states.
beats.visual_action: Cross the automated warning, route to language path, appeal, and burden reduction, then retain unequal coverage.
beats.attention_target: The appeal and unequal-coverage record.
beats.object_after: Appeal with burden and coverage residual
beats.composition: Worker left, warning center, repair and coverage right.
beats.motion_curve: Warning appears then reverses into repair rather than disappearing.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on the warning cross and appeal route.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep burden visible beside measured precision.
beats.evidence_boundary: The synthetic warning illustrates a design hazard; it does not measure language or demographic performance.

beats.narration: The participants exchange a minimized packet. One receives the incident identity and routing facts; the agency keeps sensitive records; the community group owns the notification route; corrections propagate to every earlier recipient.
beats.visual_purpose: Trace minimal sharing, local custody, community notification, and correction propagation.
beats.visual_action: Route a shared ID to agency custody and community route, then send correction to all recipients.
beats.attention_target: Correction propagation without raw-evidence centralization.
beats.composition: Shared packet left, agency/community center, correction lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Parallel custody routes followed by a single corrective propagation.
beats.camera_action: Keep local custody visible while the correction arrow travels.
beats.hold_purpose: Show federation as bounded exchange and durable correction.
beats.evidence_boundary: The packet is a proposed protocol; it does not establish lawful sharing or honest corrections.

beats.narration: A cross-jurisdiction handoff tests authority. The first platform can remove its copy, but only the agency can correct the public record and only a remedy owner can address a person's loss.
beats.visual_purpose: Keep removal, record correction, and remedy authority typed.
beats.visual_action: Route platform to remove copy, agency to correct record, and authority to remedy owner, with distinct arrows.
beats.attention_target: The three non-substitutable authority routes.
beats.composition: Platform left, agency upper right, remedy owner lower center.
beats.motion_curve: Parallel actions settle without merging into one approval.
beats.camera_action: Pan from removal to correction and finally remedy.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent takedown, correction, and remedy from borrowing authority.
beats.evidence_boundary: The synthetic handoff illustrates role separation; it does not decide jurisdiction or guarantee remedy.

beats.narration: The after-action exercise updates the playbook, rotates a detector, adds a trusted-language path, and changes the escalation deadline. Adaptation is a changed field behavior, not a sentence in a report.
beats.visual_purpose: Demonstrate adaptation as operational change.
beats.visual_action: Transform an old playbook through detector rotation, trusted-language route, deadline, and exercise into new behavior.
beats.attention_target: The green new-behavior panel.
beats.composition: Old playbook left, change fields center, new behavior right.
beats.motion_curve: Staggered updates converge into a visible state change.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on the final behavior rather than the report.
beats.hold_purpose: Make learning auditable as a changed control, not a claim of success.
beats.evidence_boundary: A changed field is not evidence that the adaptation transfers or reduces population harm.

beats.narration: Some residuals remain: an unreachable downstream copy, an unresolved dispute, or harm money cannot repair. The ledger preserves custody, next trigger, expiry, and the reason closure was not claimed.
beats.visual_purpose: Make incomplete recovery visible and owned.
beats.visual_action: Route three residuals into a ledger with custody, next trigger, expiry, and no-closure-claim fields.
beats.attention_target: The no-closure-claim field.
beats.composition: Residuals left, ledger center, ownership fields lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Parallel residual routes converge into custody without disappearing.
beats.camera_action: Widen to keep all residual categories visible.
beats.hold_purpose: Prevent closure language from erasing remaining harm.
beats.evidence_boundary: Residual custody is a design obligation, not proof of actual remedy or accountability.

beats.narration: A finite tabletop can test packet completeness, privacy minimization, role routing, pause behavior, false-positive correction, stage separation, and residual ownership. It cannot test population resilience or universal remedy.
beats.visual_purpose: State the exact ceiling of a local exercise.
beats.visual_action: Route finite checks to accept, while crossing population resilience, universal remedy, and safe society as outside the test.
beats.attention_target: The accept/reject split and crossed external claims.
beats.composition: Finite checks left, accept/reject center, untestable claims right.
beats.motion_curve: Checks assemble, then the ceiling appears as a separate state.
beats.camera_action: Hold the crossed claims in frame rather than ending on accept.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep local protocol validation separate from population outcomes.
beats.evidence_boundary: The tabletop can validate encoded transitions only; it cannot establish societal resilience, consent, safety, or universal remedy.

beats.narration: The boundary is deliberate. A fast response is not acceptable harm reduction; a takedown is not recovery; provider metrics are not societal safety; and a design rationale is not deployment evidence.
beats.visual_purpose: Close inference routes that would overread the response design.
beats.visual_action: Place response beside a vertical evidence boundary and cross speed, takedown, provider metrics, and design-to-deployment substitutions.
beats.attention_target: The evidence boundary and crossed substitutions.
beats.composition: Response left, boundary center, nonclaims right.
beats.motion_curve: Nonclaims appear one by one with visible crosses.
beats.camera_action: Keep the full boundary visible during the final cross.
beats.hold_purpose: Make evidence discipline part of the visual payoff.
beats.evidence_boundary: The derivative stays at design-rationale argument support and does not promote any safety, transfer, or ASI claim.

beats.narration: Return to Harborline. The system resists where it can, keeps services available, repairs records, learns from the miss, and leaves remaining harm visible to an accountable owner. Next, stable capability fields must carry these boundaries through model replacement.
beats.visual_purpose: Pay off the case and hand the boundaries to the next chapter.
beats.visual_action: Route Harborline to resist, service availability, repair, learning, residual owner, and the next stable-capability-fields chapter.
beats.attention_target: The accountable owner and next-chapter handoff.
beats.composition: Harborline left, outcomes center, next chapter lower right.
beats.motion_curve: Measured convergence with a final indication on the handoff.
beats.camera_action: Pull back to show the whole response without erasing residuals.
beats.hold_purpose: End with owned contestability and an explicit transfer of boundaries.
beats.evidence_boundary: Harborline is synthetic; the handoff does not establish societal resilience, acceptable residual harm, or deployment safety.
